Workflow state machine templates initialize Project machines that drive runtime entity state history
M1 delivery framework: milestone planned as waves, gates, and workstreams over the GitHub issue DAG

nodes.label: Publish iOS workflow
nodes.rationale: Manual workflow_dispatch publishing restricted to the main branch; typechecks and runs the full test suite before building so a broken build is never submitted to App Store Connect.

nodes.label: Becoming product (goal-planning and execution system)
nodes.rationale: Core idea: 'Record what you do. Shape what you become.' Turn intended outcomes into structured, executable work while keeping rules, resource constraints, and history explicit and inspectable.

nodes.label: Goal and task planning and execution capability
nodes.norm_label: goal and task planning and execution capability

nodes.label: Workflow and lifecycle management capability
nodes.rationale: Reusable, versionable Workflows define permitted lifecycle transitions; execution entities consume those rules instead of embedding ad hoc state machines.

nodes.label: Resource and budget management capability
nodes.rationale: Planned allocations and actual consumption must remain distinguishable and queryable so users can compare plans with reality.

nodes.label: Data provenance and history capability
nodes.rationale: Append-oriented structured history explains how the system reached its current state without replacing the current-state domain model; workflow changes must not silently rewrite past execution records.

nodes.label: tasks table (Task core concept)
nodes.rationale: Task rows hold only intrinsic data (title, target_description, exit_criteria); state, labels, project/goal membership, deadlines, budgets, and dependencies are deliberately externalized to relations and supporting tables.

nodes.label: workflows table (Workflow core concept)
nodes.rationale: Each row is one version of a definition; publishing freezes the row and successors form an explicit lineage chain through supersedes_id so historical execution is never rewritten.

nodes.label: resources table (Resource core concept)
nodes.rationale: Constraints (deadlines, allocations) are not intrinsic Resource fields; they are represented through core relations with metadata so any entity can be constrained by any Resource.

nodes.label: records table (Record core concept)
nodes.rationale: Records capture what actually happened (occurred_at distinct from recorded_at) with typed payloads; relationships to other core concepts live in relations, keeping the Record itself a pure occurrence fact.

nodes.label: relations table (semantic core graph)
nodes.rationale: Relations are temporal (ended_at) and carry metadata, so ending a relation preserves history and resource constraints/allocations/consumption can all be expressed as typed edges without schema changes.

nodes.label: entity_labels table (generic label assignment)
nodes.rationale: One generic temporal assignment table replaces per-entity join tables such as task_labels, so any core concept can receive any Label without new schema.

nodes.label: project_states table (Project-owned states)
nodes.rationale: source_workflow_state_id is provenance only: after initialization the Project State becomes independent, so later Workflow template edits never silently mutate an existing Project machine.

nodes.label: project_entity_states table (runtime state history)
nodes.rationale: Append-oriented state periods (entered_at/ended_at) replace in-place status columns, so current state is simply the row with ended_at IS NULL and full lifecycle history is preserved.

nodes.label: State machine identity (workflow/project + entity_type + label)
nodes.rationale: Scoping machines by workflow_id/project_id + entity_type + label_id lets different entity kinds share a Label yet follow different lifecycles, and lets Labels be pure classification when no machine is defined.

nodes.label: No foreign keys / no entities table rule
nodes.rationale: All cross-table references (workflow_id, label_id, entity_id, from/to_state_id, ...) are logical only; the application/domain layer validates them, keeping integrity rules explicit and testable in domain code rather than hidden in the database.
nodes.norm_label: no foreign keys / no entities table rule

nodes.label: SQLite port adapters (appDatabase / nodeSqliteDatabase)
nodes.rationale: Only appDatabase.ts may import expo-sqlite and only the test adapter may import node:sqlite, so tests exercise the real SQLite engine with identical SQL and transaction semantics without a device.

nodes.label: Decimal/Quantity exact quantities
nodes.rationale: bigint-mantissa exact decimals persisted as canonical TEXT never pass through binary floating point; combining Quantities with different units is a domain error, never an implicit conversion.

nodes.label: Project-owned state machine independence
nodes.rationale: A selected applicable Workflow is copied into a Project-owned machine so later template edits do not rewrite the Project's execution rules.

nodes.label: Temporal relations and versioned planning metadata
nodes.rationale: Budget/allocation changes end the prior relation and append a successor rather than overwriting, keeping planned amounts distinguishable from actual consumption.
nodes.norm_label: temporal relations and versioned planning metadata

nodes.label: Append-oriented provenance Records
nodes.rationale: Corrections are later Records with negative aggregation effect, not edits; the Record table is never treated as a mutable event-sourced replacement for current-state aggregates.

nodes.label: withTransaction unit-of-work boundary
nodes.rationale: The only sanctioned unit-of-work boundary: a mutation and its provenance/history writes commit or roll back atomically in one transaction.

nodes.label: Schema encoding rules (no FK, TEXT encodings)
nodes.rationale: Persistence may reinforce uniqueness and value constraints (PKs, CHECKs) but never referential integrity; UUIDs/datetimes/JSON stored as TEXT, booleans as INTEGER 0/1, so the domain layer remains the single source of integrity logic.
nodes.norm_label: schema encoding rules (no fk, text encodings)

nodes.label: CI pipeline (currently disabled)
nodes.rationale: The pipeline was removed to speed up the M1 implementation loop; validation runs locally via npm run typecheck and npm test, to be restored after M1.

nodes.label: SemVer release tagging and GitHub Releases
nodes.norm_label: semver release tagging and github releases

nodes.label: iOS publishing procedure (TestFlight / App Store)
nodes.rationale: Build numbers are managed remotely by EAS (appVersionSource: remote with autoIncrement) so repeated builds never collide; the marketing version comes from app.json. The initial distribution certificate must be bootstrapped interactively because non-interactive runners cannot create signing credentials.

nodes.label: Milestone V1 Domain Foundation
nodes.rationale: Deferred scope is explicit: M1 is not billing, general accounting, scheduling, automated budget remediation, or a full audit UI — the durable plans, usage, records, and query services are designed so those can be added without changing historical meaning.

nodes.label: Definition of ready / definition of done
nodes.rationale: GitHub's native sub-issue and blocked-by relationships are the source of truth for scheduling; the plan document must never silently override an open blocker, keeping dependency changes auditable.
nodes.norm_label: definition of ready / definition of done
